payer: Brands and retailers pay a per-unit fee to run the exchange (who funds the exchange bonus: UNKNOWN; Croma says the brand's terms govern = PROXY that brands fund it). The buyer of the collected unit (recycler, refurbisher) pays for the device.
unit_economics: LG/Attero exchange values paid to customers (FACT): split AC under 2T Rs5,000 working / Rs4,500 dead; double-door fridge 250-350L Rs2,000/1,100; top-load WM Rs1,200/900. A dead AC is worth Rs4,500 against Rs3,500 scrap (FACT, prior); the gap is about one EPR certificate (40 kg x Rs22 = Rs880, DERIVED, weight ASSUMPTION). Keepwell as operator: fee plus spread Rs300-600 a unit (ASSUMPTION); logistics Rs60-100 a unit if batched on technician routes vs about Rs500 for a one-off Tata Ace trip with a helper (DERIVED from Porter base Rs200-230 plus Rs14-18/km LOW). Contribution Rs200-450 a unit (DERIVED).
gross_margin: On net fee revenue: 50-75% (DERIVED). On gross revenue if Keepwell buys and resells the device: 8-16% (PROXY: Cashify gross margin of about 15.7%, DERIVED in prior work).
capital_need: Low if asset-light: no warehouse, same-day handover to a recycler or refurbisher. Working capital is about 7-14 days of payouts: Rs3-8 L per cluster (ASSUMPTION). If principal: a 500-1,000 sq ft yard per cluster (cost UNKNOWN).
india_market_size_cr: Device value pool Rs875-1,750 Cr a year; fee pool Rs105-210 Cr (DERIVED: about 35 mn large units a year [AC 11.1-11.5 mn FACT ICRA FY26; WM 10.3 mn PROXY; fridge 13.8 mn 2022 PROXY] x 10-20% exchange share ASSUMPTION x Rs2,500 average value, or x Rs300 fee). Exchange share UNKNOWN; Flipkart forecast 20% in 2021, outcome never reported.
comparables: India: Selsmart by Attero (Rs100 Cr run-rate, 30k orders a month, 25+ cities, Aug 2025; Rs500 Cr target for Mar 2026, result UNKNOWN); Digi2L (Bosch partner since Jan 2023, 20-30k customers claimed, revenue about $76k LOW, investors Onsitego and Panasonic Ignition); Cashify (FY25 Rs1,096 Cr, last valuation Rs1,980 Cr in 2022, IPO planned for 2027); Flipkart exchange. Global: Recommerce Group (bought Verkaufen.ch in 2025, financials UNKNOWN).
time_to_first_cr: Net basis: about 3,300 exchanges at Rs300 is too few; it needs about 33,000 exchanges, so year 3-4 at roughly 12 clusters (DERIVED). Gross basis: about 3,300 units at Rs3,000, so year 1-2.
network_advantage: Strong. The old unit is uninstalled during the new-unit install visit, so there is no separate trip; cluster runs batch pickups; the per-appliance record gives the model, age and service history for remote grading before pickup, which cuts the re-quote and dispute rate (rate UNKNOWN). The retailer relationship provides the point-of-sale trigger.

payer: First Keepwell's own jobs: the household pays a parts price, Keepwell earns the parts margin. Then third-party agencies, independent technicians and parts distributors pay a parts margin plus software (Rs1-3k per agency a month, ASSUMPTION).
unit_economics: Customer prices (FACT, UC card): capacitor Rs599-749; fan motor Rs2,299; PCB repair Rs1,500-4,500; 1.5T compressor Rs8,500. Distributor or dealer margin 15-40% (PROXY LOW, prior). Per cluster: 12,480 jobs x 40% needing parts (ASSUMPTION) x Rs1,500 average parts ticket (ASSUMPTION) = Rs75 L parts revenue a year; at 20% margin = Rs15 L gross profit (DERIVED).
gross_margin: Parts 15-25% (PROXY/ASSUMPTION); software 70-80% (ASSUMPTION). Blended contribution after holding, obsolescence and returns: about 8-12% (ASSUMPTION).
capital_need: Inventory of about 60 days of fast movers = about Rs10 L per cluster (DERIVED: Rs75 L x 80% COGS x 60/365). Slow movers (PCBs, compressors) ordered per job. One shared regional stock room per 3-5 clusters (rent UNKNOWN). Distributor credit terms UNKNOWN.
india_market_size_cr: Out-of-warranty parts pool about Rs2,400-4,900 Cr (DERIVED: repair-services market $0.98 bn 2023 PROXY BlueWeave x Rs83 = Rs8,140 Cr x 30-60% parts share of the bill, DERIVED prior). In-warranty parts flow through brand depots: UNKNOWN.
comparables: India appliance parts: no funded pure-play found. Note SparesHub and Boodmo are AUTO parts (Boodmo about $12-14M raised, revenue UNKNOWN; SparesHub about Rs2.8 Cr FY25 LOW); Koovers (auto B2B parts) FY25 Rs198 Cr revenue, Rs36 Cr loss; Garaaz Rs4.55 Cr seed. Brand ASC/depot network (margins UNKNOWN); IndiaMART compatible-parts sellers. Global: Marcone (Genstar buyout 2021, 113 locations, price undisclosed), Reliable Parts (bought Automatic Appliance Parts in May 2025 and AMRE in Sep 2025), Appliance Parts Pros (UNKNOWN).
time_to_first_cr: Rs1 Cr of parts revenue from about 1.3 cluster-years of own jobs, so year 1-2 (DERIVED). Rs1 Cr of gross profit: about 7 cluster-years, so year 3 (DERIVED).
network_advantage: Strongest fit. The per-appliance record predicts which part a job needs before the visit (first-time-fix rate up, fewer second trips); demand pooled across clusters is bargaining power with distributors; failure-by-model data is the 'intelligence' product. Distribution rides on technician routes.

payer: Price-sensitive Tier 2/3 buyers, landlords, PGs and hostels pay the resale price. Third-party refurbishers pay a listing or transaction fee if Keepwell runs a marketplace.
unit_economics: AC (DERIVED): buy Rs5,000 (LG exchange level) + refurbishment Rs1,000-2,500 (ASSUMPTION, prior) + gas and parts about Rs1,000 (ASSUMPTION) + logistics Rs300-500 + warranty reserve about 5% (ASSUMPTION) + reinstall about Rs800 = about Rs8,800-10,500 against a sell price of Rs12,000-18,000 (PROXY: Delhi refurbished split AC from Rs17,999 with install and 1-year replacement LOW; IndiaMART used split Rs10-16k). Fridge: buy Rs2,000 + Rs1,500 cost = Rs3,500 against Rs5,500-5,700 refurbished with warranty on OLX Delhi (PROXY). WM resale price UNKNOWN. Marketplace take: 10-14% (PROXY Back Market).
gross_margin: Principal: 15-35% gross (DERIVED; prior estimate about 15%). Marketplace: about 12-14% take on GMV (PROXY Back Market). Costify (Delhi) about Rs4 Cr revenue, margin UNKNOWN.
capital_need: High. Stock of about 100 units x Rs7-9k = Rs7-9 L per cluster; a workshop with gas-charging and vacuum kit Rs3-5 L capex (ASSUMPTION); yard rent UNKNOWN; warranty float. AC buying and selling both peak Mar-Jun, so turns are fast in season and stock is dead in Oct-Dec.
india_market_size_cr: Rs600-2,600 Cr (DERIVED: 3.5-7 mn exchanges x 30% refurbishable ASSUMPTION x Rs6,000-13,000 resale). The C2C used market (OLX) is UNKNOWN.
comparables: India: Zefo (bought by Quikr for about Rs200-210 Cr in 2019, now dormant or absorbed); Costify about Rs4 Cr; Cashify does not refurbish large appliances; RentoMojo spends about Rs400 per unit on refurbishment (mostly furniture). Global: Back Market GMV $/EUR3.5 bn 2025, EBITDA-positive, valued at $5.7 bn in 2022 (about 11.5x Sacra-estimated 2025 revenue of $495M, DERIVED and stale); Refurbed EUR93.3M revenue 2025, raised EUR50M Oct 2025, valuation UNKNOWN; Beko second-life sells up to 30% below retail; Bosch Premium Refurbished (Netherlands); Electrolux Professional R+vive.
time_to_first_cr: At about Rs13k a unit, about 770 units: year 2 once trade-in flows (DERIVED). Rs1 Cr of gross profit takes about 3,000+ units: year 3-4.
network_advantage: Medium-strong on supply: trade-ins give first look at units with a known service history (grading data); in-house technicians do the refurbishment in trough months (Oct-Dec), using spare capacity; installs and warranty service are done by the same network. The weak point is demand: small-town buyers of used goods buy C2C.

payer: Producers (brands) pay recyclers for EPR certificates; PROs earn a fee for arranging compliance; collectors earn scrap value plus a handling fee (fee UNKNOWN). Retailers pay little or nothing.
unit_economics: EPR floor Rs22/kg = 30% of environmental compensation; ceiling = 100% (about Rs74/kg for consumer electronics) (FACT). Per unit at the floor: AC about 40 kg = Rs880; fridge about 45 kg = Rs990; WM about 30 kg = Rs660 (weights ASSUMPTION). Certificates go to the RECYCLER, not the collector (FACT, prior). Keepwell's handling share Rs2-6/kg = Rs80-240 a unit (ASSUMPTION); scrap spread on an AC is about Rs0-500 (ASSUMPTION). Recycling cost Rs6-20/kg (FACT, CEAMA estimate).
gross_margin: Recyclers: Attero EBITDA 3.2%, Namo about 12%, Ecoreco 22-70% (FACT via India Forum). Collector with a fee only: 40-60% on the fee (ASSUMPTION), but rupees a unit are small.
capital_need: Low if Keepwell is a collection point feeding a registered recycler or PRO. Registration as a dismantler or recycler is out of scope (a 500 t/yr unit needs about Rs65 L capex and Rs36 L working capital, ASSUMPTION from a project report).
india_market_size_cr: Certificate market at the floor: Rs3,080 Cr upper bound; at the ceiling Rs10,360 Cr (DERIVED: 1.4 mn t generated FY25 FACT x Rs22-74/kg; actual obligations are based on past sales, so the true figure is lower). Large-appliance share UNKNOWN.
comparables: Attero FY25 Rs961 Cr, PAT Rs14.6 Cr, over 30% of the EPR certificate market, FY26 target Rs2,000 Cr, Temasek pre-IPO talks (headline); Recykal FY25 Rs978 Cr, FY26 Rs1,498 Cr, about $280M valuation; Karo Sambhav FY25 about Rs150 Cr operating income, PAT about Rs1 Cr (single source), Rs56 Cr pre-Series A (Rainmatter, Jun 2026); Namo eWaste SME IPO Sep 2024 Rs51.2 Cr at Rs85, listed about Rs162-170, FY25 Rs151 Cr; Ecoreco FY26 Rs48.2 Cr revenue, PAT Rs22.9 Cr, market cap about Rs850-930 Cr (about 18-19x revenue, DERIVED); Hulladek (PRO, 2,050 t in 2023). Global: Sims Lifecycle Services underlying EBIT A$32.6M FY25, FY26 guidance A$170-175M.
time_to_first_cr: At about Rs160 a unit handling: about 62,000 units, year 5+ (DERIVED). On a gross scrap pass-through basis: about 2,900 ACs, year 1, but about 5% margin.
network_advantage: Real but small. Every service visit meets an end-of-life unit; the appliance record creates a traceable chain of custody (the audit-grade data that brands' compliance teams and CPCB audits want after fake-certificate scandals). Value is as a feeder to the trade-in and refurbishment layers and as brand goodwill, not as profit.

payer: OEM and ODM manufacturers (Amber, EPACK, PG Electroplast, Dixon, Voltas-Beko, PLI component makers) pay under enterprise contracts for line inspection. Brands might pay for field-reliability analytics.
unit_economics: Contract size per line in India UNKNOWN (ASSUMPTION Rs10-30 L a year per line). LandingLens: Free and $50/mo self-serve tiers, Enterprise custom (FACT). SwitchOn: about $2.1M revenue (LOW) across 170+ lines and 60+ plants, about Rs1 L per line a year if all paying (DERIVED, LOW).
gross_margin: Software 60-75%; lower with cameras and integration (ASSUMPTION; no Indian vendor discloses).
capital_need: High in capability, not cash: a computer-vision and machine-learning team, integration engineers, hardware partners, 6-18 month pilots (ASSUMPTION; sales cycle UNKNOWN).
india_market_size_cr: India machine-vision market $0.63 bn 2025 (IMARC PROXY) = about Rs5,300 Cr at Rs85 (ASSUMPTION FX); estimates range $0.63-1.2 bn. Appliance-manufacturing slice UNKNOWN. Context: Amber FY26 revenue Rs12,186 Cr; EPACK FY26 AC revenue Rs1,046 Cr; PGEL room-AC revenue Rs3,288 Cr; PLI white goods 85 firms, Rs11,198 Cr committed investment, Rs6,238 Cr outlay.
comparables: India: SwitchOn ($8M pre-Series B 2026, $13.3M total), Frinks AI ($5.4M pre-Series A), Qualitas Technologies (undisclosed accelerator rounds, about 31 staff), Kanerika (IT services firm with an inspection agent; revenue UNKNOWN), Akridata (about $8M revenue LOW). Global: Instrumental (about $80M raised, $50M Series C 2022, NVentures 2026), Elementary ($30M Series B Dec 2021, $47.5M total), Landing AI ($57M Series A 2021, ABB strategic). Multiples UNKNOWN (all private).
time_to_first_cr: With 3-4 lines at about Rs30 L each, about 2-3 years after hiring a CV team, given pilot cycles (ASSUMPTION).
network_advantage: Weak for inspection, moderate for reliability data. Field failures by model, component, age and region are a real signal that factories do not see after the warranty ends. But brands already have warranty-claim data from their ASC networks; Keepwell's sample is small-town and out-of-warranty, and turning it into line-level defect prevention needs serial-number linkage the ODMs control. The data could be sold as reliability analytics to brands; the camera product does not fit.
